No, that is not true. The Swiss Confederation did not adopt its first constitution in 1291, nor does the original document from that year remain in force today.

The famous **Federal Charter of 1291** is considered the founding document of the Old Swiss Confederacy, but it was a simple alliance pact among a few cantons (originally Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden) to maintain peace and defend their liberties. It was not a constitution in the modern sense, and it certainly does not remain unchanged to this day.

Switzerland's modern constitutional framework began to take shape in the 19th century. The first federal constitution of the modern Swiss state was adopted in 1848, after the Sonderbund War and the establishment of the federal state. This constitution has been revised several times since then (notably in 1874, 1971, and most recently in 1999), reflecting changes in society, politics, and law. The current constitution, adopted in 1999, is the one currently in force.
